name: Ascaris lumbricoides

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Fertilized egg: about 45–75 µm long, thick-shelled and often brown with a mammillated coat. Decorticated eggs lack this outer texture.
Unfertilized eggs are more elongated, sometimes up to 90 µm long, with a thinner shell and disorganized granules. Adults are large cylindrical worms.

transmission.detail: Eggs embryonate in soil; ingested infective eggs release larvae that migrate through liver and lungs before returning to the intestine to mature.

life_cycle.detail: Eggs pass in stool; fertile eggs develop in suitable soil.
Larvae hatch, migrate to the lungs, ascend airways, and are swallowed.
Adults mature in the small intestine and females produce eggs.

hosts: Definitive: humans; closely related pig Ascaris can complicate species attribution. No intermediate host.
distribution: Worldwide, especially warm regions with inadequate sanitation, including Southeast Asia.
clinical_significance: Heavy worm burdens can impair nutrition or obstruct the intestine; migrating worms may enter biliary ducts and larval migration can cause pulmonary symptoms.
specimen: Fertilized or unfertilized eggs in stool; adult worms may be passed.
diagnostics: Stool wet mount/concentration at 100–400×; record fertilization and coat state separately.
differential_diagnosis: Decorticated eggs can resemble other smooth eggs. Pig-associated Ascaris cannot be confidently separated by routine egg morphology.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated
description: Ascaris lumbricoides — Large intestinal roundworm. Heavy worm burdens can impair nutrition or obstruct the intestine; migrating worms may enter biliary ducts and larval migration can cause pulmonary symptoms.

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
